title: Secrets Underground

beats.narrativeText: Restoring power opens a section of Outpost Echo nobody has set foot in for years: an underground geological survey area.

The landscape surrounding the station isn't as ordinary as it looked from above — and whatever's unusual about it might explain observations from missions that seemed to have nothing to do with geology at all.
The learner examines the rock samples the expedition collected and compares the geological layers preserved down here.
beats.trigger: Rock samples examined and layers compared

beats.narrativeText: Interpreting the expedition's own survey maps starts to give the surrounding landscape a real shape — not just rock, but a structure with a story.
The learner must explain their findings using the samples, the layers and the maps all together — no single one of them tells the full story alone.
The unusual geology isn't just interesting on its own — it turns out to have quietly shaped decisions the expedition made in missions the learner has already completed.
The learner reflects on how much the environment itself — not just the expedition's choices — shaped the research happening at Outpost Echo.
With the environmental context finally uncovered, several observations that never quite made sense before suddenly do.

activities.title: Examine Rock Samples
activities.storyContext: An underground geological survey area has become accessible for the first time, and the expedition's own rock samples are still exactly where they left them.
activities.instructions: Examine the rock samples the expedition collected and note their properties — the same careful approach as Mission 9's samples, applied here.
activities.output: Notes on the properties of each rock sample.

activities.title: Compare Geological Layers
activities.storyContext: The surrounding landscape contains unusual geological features — visible if you compare the layers carefully rather than glancing at them.
activities.instructions: Compare the layers visible in the survey area and note anything unusual about how they're arranged.

activities.title: Interpret Survey Maps
activities.storyContext: The expedition's own survey maps hold real clues about the shape of the surrounding landscape, if you know how to read them.
activities.instructions: Interpret the survey maps to understand the layout of the geological features they record.
activities.output: An interpretation of the survey maps.

activities.title: Explain Findings Using Evidence
activities.storyContext: The geological features may explain several previously unexplained observations — but only if you draw on more than one source of evidence at once.
activities.instructions: Explain what your findings reveal, using evidence from the samples, layers and maps together, not just whichever one feels most convincing.
activities.output: A written explanation supported by combined evidence.

activities.title: Produce a Geological Field Sketch
activities.storyContext: A field sketch would help future Explorers understand the survey area at a glance.
activities.instructions: Produce a geological field sketch of the surrounding area, labelling key features.

activities.title: Studying Landscapes Without Disturbing Them
activities.storyContext: Geologists study landscapes carefully, without damaging them.
activities.instructions: Find out how geologists study landscapes without disturbing them.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: How did the landscape around the station affect the expedition's earlier decisions, and which earlier mission does that connect to most clearly?

discussionPoints: What surprised you about the landscape around the station?
How did the geology help explain earlier expedition decisions?
parentGuide.preparation: No special preparation required; real rocks or stones can be used to practise comparing properties if available.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for findings explained using evidence from the samples, layers and maps together, not just one source.

completionCriteria: Rock samples examined, geological layers compared, and findings explained using evidence.
